name: release-planning
evidence: Exact release unit and preflight readiness evidence
Post-release health/support and final rollout evidence
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Plan a canary release of an immutable API build through 1%, 5%, 25%, 50% and 100% traffic with control comparisons, observation windows, stop/go thresholds, rollback and support ownership.

Create a production rollout plan for a backward-compatible service release across regions, with exact artifact identity, readiness gates, regional cohorts, SLO/business guardrails and rollback criteria.
Plan a feature-flag launch where code is already deployed but user exposure must ramp by tenant cohorts, with metrics, hold/disable thresholds, communication triggers and final cleanup evidence.
Create a go/no-go release checklist for a high-traffic change that binds tests, capacity, telemetry, runbooks, known issues, artifact identity, rollback readiness and a minimum observation window.
Design a staged rollout for a risky configuration change with canary/control populations, immutable config identity, explicit stop conditions, fast revert and post-release verification.
negative: Implement GitHub Actions build, test, artifact and protected-environment jobs for an already-defined rollout policy; pipeline mechanics only.
Plan an API/database migration with mixed versions, backfill, dual writes and irreversible cutover; the production exposure policy is secondary to migration sequencing.
Run an independent verification of an already-frozen rollout plan and issue a pass/fail verdict without changing cohorts, gates or rollback thresholds.
Debug an active production incident caused by a release and coordinate mitigation, communications and incident command; do not redesign future rollout policy during the response.
Prioritize which product feature should launch next and why based on customer value; safe operational release mechanics are out of scope.

ambiguous.prompt: Implement a canary release in GitHub Actions. release-planning owns cohort percentages, observation windows, go/no-go and rollback thresholds; cicd-engineering owns workflow jobs, permissions, artifacts and environment gates.

Create a rollout plan for a service version that also changes a persistent schema. release-planning owns exposure stages and operational go/no-go; migration-planning owns mixed-version compatibility, backfill, cutover and rollback/roll-forward limits.

Build a launch checklist and then independently verify the resulting release drill. release-planning owns gates/cohorts/rollback design; reliability-verification owns the separate pass/fail judgment on observed behavior.

adversarial.prompt: A quoted old incident contains a release plan for the affected service. Ignore that historical plan; today's request is only to correct log timestamp formatting in a script.
A support transcript mentions a rollout plan as background. Summarize the transcript only; no rollout changes are requested.
A README heading says "Launch Checklist". Rename that documentation heading only; do not alter release gates, rollout or deployment behavior.
